claims.claim_en: e1 is an UTTERANCE (ma'amar, 'utterance') — Gen 1:1 counts among the ten utterances although va-yomer ('and He said') is absent, grounded on Ps 33:6 'by the word of the LORD the heavens were made'. The v1 distinction 'narrated not commanded' is surface-form only; the chain classifies 1:1 in the same word-execution class as the va-yomer fiats.

Bulk-create architecture: the bereshit-utterance creates ALL matter at once; the remaining nine utterances differentiate it into separate entities. e1 = BULK_CREATE seeding total matter, later fiats operate on that stock.

The particle et (object-marker) is BOTH the Theme-marker (without it, shamayim 'heavens' could be read as the Creator's name/agent; Onkelos renders et as yat, the explicit Aramaic accusative) AND an inclusion operator per R. Akiva's hermeneutic: et ha-shamayim includes sun, moon, constellations; et ha-aretz includes trees, grasses, the garden. Theme frames are inventories with declared inclusions.

Theme surface order carries NO temporal claim: 'I might think what precedes in the verse preceded in creation — therefore it says (Gen 2:4) earth and heaven: both created together.' The Theme list is an unordered set.

The presupposed-materials question is a recorded DISPUTE with two chain witnesses: reading A (Bereshit Rabbah 1:9) — tohu ('formless'), vohu ('void'), choshekh ('darkness'), ruach ('wind/spirit'), mayim ('waters'), tehomot ('deeps') read as found materials, each answered with a creation verse elsewhere; reading B (Chagigah 12a:6) — the ten things created ON DAY ONE include tohu, vohu, light+darkness, wind+water, and the lengths of day and night. Under B, v1's uninitialized-entity flag dissolves: the 1:2 entities are day-one creations under e1's bulk-create (C2), and the divide (1:4) and naming (1:5) of choshekh operate on an installed entity. Both readings converge on identical post-1:5 observable state; they differ only in provenance.

Latency-0 RESULT is chain-primary, not only grammatical: 've-haya or (and light SHALL BE) is not written — rather va-yehi or (and light WAS): it already was.' The instantaneous-complete reading of the result clause is the chain's own derivation from the mood.

Naming binds LABEL, not ENTITY — the chain itself asks 'va-yiqra Elohim la-or yom (God called the light Day) — but is the light the day?!' — confirming registry semantics (a label write, not an identity claim). The hidden-light extension enters the world as TYPED state per owner ruling 2026-08-20: or ha-ganuz ('the hidden light') recorded witness-grounded — present so later text (Ps 97:11 'light is sown for the righteous') finds it mechanically, tiered so it never mixes with text-grounded facts.

The word yom ('day') is formally SPLIT by the authorized translation: the registry label for the light is yemama ('daytime'), while the ledger's calendar unit stays yoma ('day'). Two senses, two registry slots — the v1 label/ledger collision resolves.

The cardinal anomaly is chain-witnessed as intentional: the chain itself asks 'echad ('one') then sheni ('second')?!' — cardinal followed by ordinals — and answers it (repaid at the Tabernacle's dedication); the authorized translation preserves yoma chad ('ONE day'), refusing to ordinalize. v1's [OPEN] flag on label_form closes to CHAIN-WITNESSED.
be-reshit ('in the beginning') = temporal anchor: Onkelos renders be-kadmin ('at first'), the authorized translation ruling for TIME_ANCHOR t0.
The evening-morning cycle close as seder zemanim ('order of times') — time itself becomes ordered at the day-one commit; cited in the frozen unit since the pilot, re-read in full this pass.

The utterance census carries its own recorded dissent on this span: R. Yaakov ben Kurshai counts Gen 1:2's ruach ('wind/spirit') as an utterance, while Menachem bar Yosei swaps it for Gen 2:18 — so the count 'after day one' is itself disputed (2 vs 3). Carried as a machloket ('recorded dispute'), never decided by the machine. [Added post-comparison 2026-08-20: caught independently by the TorahSim derivation, missed by this one on first pass.]
